hypotheses.content: Loading associations depend on molecular environment and PE/EA and differ between endpoints. Several matched series show declining V1 with relatively stable or increasing V2, while exceptions and curved responses preclude a universal loading shift.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Many eligible predictions change very little with amount. Matched boundaries and selected interior points can teach endpoint-specific response shape and establish where corrections transfer across common chemical families.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which missing amount segments are flat, monotonic or curved? Do the m96 and m74 boundaries support an interior maximum, and does the m92 middle-amount pattern reproduce?

hypotheses.content: The broad pure-EA completion of m197 does not warrant a blanket phenolic V2 correction. The shorter m117 and m186 responses extend into weaker eluent, and m105 remains short at the newly measured intermediate ratio. Transfer must remain graph- and condition-dependent.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Recent completion overpredictions for m117 show that a strong-eluent correction alone did not specify its weaker-eluent curve. Adjacent ratio and amount measurements can define the limits of transfer among donor-containing aromatic graphs.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How do the missing m117 low-amount 5/1 and m197 middle-amount 20/1 points connect their curves, and does the strong onset amount association in m209 attenuate at 5/1?

hypotheses.content: Recorded loading-volume associations are conditional. Matched m168 records show small onset differences and modest completion differences, whereas some m125 comparisons between 300 and 500 uL show much larger endpoint changes. These observations do not identify a general mechanism or justify ignoring loading volume.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Current matched-volume predictions are nearly identical. An exact contrast at another ratio tests whether this insensitivity is appropriate, while an m125 interior point constrains interpolation within a distinct recorded protocol. Unrecorded factors may contribute to the observed differences.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At m168 10/1 and fixed sample amount, does changing recorded DCM volume from 300 to 400 uL retain the small completion difference seen at 1/1 and 5/1? Does m125 pure-EA interpolation remain short within the 300-uL protocol?

hypotheses.content: The mild completion amount association recently measured for ortho-nitro aldehyde m198 at 20/1 need not transfer unchanged across solvent ratios or to other nitro-carbonyl environments. The para-nitro aldehyde series has a substantially different completion association under its own recorded protocol.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A shared correction based on nitro and carbonyl counts could obscure positional, structural and protocol dependence. Fixed-molecule amount contrasts test ratio dependence without assigning differences between molecules solely to substitution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m198 at 10/1 retain the modest completion change and onset decline seen at 20/1, and does the m37 5/1 high-amount point show a different boundary to this behavior?

feedback_interpretation: The latest alcohol midpoint labels substantially reduce the urgency of further 10/1 interpolation: m135 and m60 were predicted within about 1 mL for both endpoints. I move those tests to other ratios and structural environments. The m4 high-amount labels at 10/1 and 20/1 finished at 22.59 and 23.55 mL, rejecting the predicted trough; its selected midpoint now tests loading curvature after that correction. The m81 20/1 high-amount completion of 23.55 rejects a uniformly short high-amount surface, while conflicting earlier same-tuple outcomes still prevent a sharp mechanistic interpretation. For m82, both new 2/1 boundaries finished near 20 mL, so the large completion decline at 5/1 is not a general loading law. The m198 20/1 labels had only a small completion increase with amount and were both shorter than their acquisition predictions, motivating an adjacent-ratio contrast rather than another weak-boundary extension. m117 again finished earlier than predicted at both 20/1 and 50/1, whereas m105 at 5/1 was close to prediction; this further limits broad phenolic transfer. The m142 50/1 high-amount finish of 30.27 mL exposed an additional completion miss, so I test its neighboring 20/1 boundary alongside m134. The m51 midpoint showed earlier onset with almost unchanged completion relative to its low-amount reference, motivating a stronger-eluent transfer test. The new m168 volume contrast had exactly matching onset and a small completion difference, supporting another exact contrast rather than assuming a large generic injection-volume effect. The m211 low-amount 10/1 result was relatively ordinary and does not establish repeatability of its unusual 50/1 outcome. Historical errors are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch uses existing observations as experimental anchors and reserves paired new measurements for questions that a single label cannot answer. The m198, m26, m96 and m74 amount pairs distinguish response shape from a graph-level retention correction. Alcohol and basic-aromatic interior or boundary points test transfer of endpoint-specific loading associations after the latest midpoint successes. Phenolic measurements define where recent completion corrections should apply, while m4, m142 and m81 address specific newly exposed or revised failure regions. The exact m168 loading-volume pair probes a recorded condition that current predictions barely distinguish; m125 constrains interpolation within another protocol. One m92 repeat is justified by an unusual measured middle-amount pattern whose reproducibility affects interpretation of related ester curves. The m18 pure-EA measurement addresses invalid predicted endpoint ordering in an otherwise short-retention region. All selected graphs already occur in the observations, so exploration concerns uncovered condition relationships and transfer boundaries. I avoid redundant candidate IDs representing identical tuples except for the deliberate measured-tuple repeat. Quantile widths from this single predictor are not treated as epistemic uncertainty; the supplied V2 lower quantiles frequently equal zero, limiting their value for ranking. CW distance is secondary to the scientific contrasts. These labels may improve generalization by constraining how structure, solvent strength, amount and loading volume jointly affect V1 and V2 across related rows. They do not target maximal retention or narrow experimental intervals, and V2 minus V1 is not used as uncertainty.
